label: Весёлый / Грустный
description: Весёлый vs грустный: cheerful/sad contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Весёлый' takes the masculine ending to match 'сосед'. The everyday phrase anchors the form in a familiar context.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Грустная' takes the feminine ending to match 'музыка'. The sentence places the form in a vivid everyday scene.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Весёлое' takes the neuter ending to match 'лето'. The fond memory makes the neuter form concrete.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Грустные' takes the plural ending to match 'глаза'. The vivid image fixes the plural form in mind.
Strategic focus: Direct contrast across genders. 'Весёлый' is masculine nominative for 'мальчик' while 'грустную' is feminine accusative for 'сестру'. The scene pairs both adjectives in one action.
Strategic focus: Masculine predicate adjective. 'Грустный' follows the noun as a predicate describing 'фильм'. The everyday remark roots the form in daily life.
Strategic focus: Feminine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'была', 'весёлой' takes the feminine instrumental ending to match 'песня'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'грустными' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'лица'. The sentence extends the pattern into the plural.
Strategic focus: Short-form masculine predicate. The short form 'грустен' states a present mood of the subject with a vowel-fill 'е'. Short forms are typical when describing a current state.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Веселее' is the comparative of 'весёлый' and stays the same for any gender. The sentence reports a shift in the party's mood.
